nodes.label: outline HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: Chart ingress and HTTPRoute are both disabled because Outline is exposed exclusively through the Cloudflare Tunnel Ingress; WEB_CONCURRENCY is forced to 1 to override the .env value of 4 so scaling happens via replicas instead of in-pod throng forks, keeping per-component memory ~4x lower.

nodes.label: outline web component (web,websockets,worker,cron)
nodes.rationale: web, websockets, worker and cron run in one process because websockets has no WEBSOCKETS_URL and an isolated worker/cron leaks memory unbounded (BullMQ leak when run alone); cron duplication across 2 replicas is safe since BullMQ repeatable jobs are idempotent.

nodes.label: outline collaboration component
nodes.rationale: Runs separately because it has its own URL/path and needs independent scaling; multi-replica collaboration requires REDIS_COLLABORATION_URL in outline-env.

nodes.label: Outline Postgres connection pool sizing (MIN=1/MAX=3)
nodes.rationale: Postgres max_connections is 100 cluster-wide; with ~9 component pods the .env default MIN=5/MAX=10 exhausts it. The CNPG pooler is session-mode so it cannot multiplex these away, hence a small per-pod pool (9 x 3 = 27 max).

nodes.label: reposilite-cloudflare-tunnel Ingress (repo.onelitefeather.dev)
nodes.rationale: backend-protocol annotation set to http because reposilite serves plain HTTP on 8080; the controller takes over the existing CNAME and flips it to proxied automatically.

nodes.label: reposilite HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: priorityClassName feather-standard is injected via a post-render kustomize patch because the chart exposes no field for it; JAVA_OPTS heap bumped from 64M to 256M because the OTel javaagent's SDK buffers/batching need headroom on top of Reposilite's baseline.

nodes.label: otel-agent init container (Java agent jar sidecar copy)
nodes.rationale: Follows the otis/vulpes-backend pattern: an init container copies the OTel Java agent jar into an emptyDir the main container mounts read-only, since the app image ships no agent.

nodes.label: logs.onelitefeather.net/format=ansi log pipeline opt-in
nodes.rationale: Reposilite's console logger emits ANSI SGR color codes with no JSON option, so the pod opts into the alloy-logs ANSI-strip + level-extract stage; OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER stays 'none' because stdout already ships via container-stdout -> alloy-logs -> Loki and OTLP logs would duplicate it.

nodes.label: shlink HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: All shlink config is passed generically via env now that the chart carries no bespoke .Values.shlink.*; chart ingress and HTTPRoute are off because exposure runs through the Cloudflare Tunnel Ingress.

nodes.label: shlink REDIS_SERVERS direct-URI Dragonfly connection
nodes.rationale: Dragonfly cutover uses a single DIRECT connection (no Sentinel) because the operator keeps the `dragonfly` Service pointed at the current master. In standalone mode shlink-common's RedisFactory::resolveOptions only applies REDIS_SERVERS_PASSWORD for sentinel, so the password must be embedded in the URI; the whole URI (with password and DB 8) therefore lives in the secret to stay out of git. See docs/dragonfly-redis-cutover.md.

nodes.label: uptime-kuma HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: The dirsigler uptime-kuma chart copies podLabels into the (immutable) Deployment selector, so adding the Loki env label via podLabels breaks upgrades; it is injected into the pod template only via a post-render kustomize patch. ServiceMonitor basic-auth credentials come from a Secret via valuesFrom targetPath so they stay out of git.

nodes.label: loki HelmRelease (Distributed deploymentMode)
nodes.rationale: SimpleScalable targets (write/read/backend) are explicitly zeroed because the chart defaults them to 3 replicas each and validate.yaml rejects mixed scalable + distributed replica counts. replication_factor matches ingester.replicas=3 so every write is fully replicated; exactly one compactor may run at a time.

nodes.label: Loki 100MiB gRPC max message size override
nodes.rationale: The default 4MiB gRPC message size was too small for larger query results (querier -> query-scheduler/-frontend), producing 'grpc: received message larger than max' / ResourceExhausted. frontend_worker is a top-level config key (Loki's root Config embeds worker.Config there), not nested under querier. Querier and query-frontend memory limits were raised afterwards because letting 100MiB responses through OOM-killed them at the old 512Mi limit.

nodes.label: Loki discover_service_name label priority
nodes.rationale: Grafana's service picker keys off service_name, which Loki derives from the first matching label. Chart-shared apps all land under app="micronaut", so `instance` (the Helm release name, e.g. otis) is prioritised ahead of `app` to give each release its own service identity.

nodes.label: mimir HelmRelease (mimir-distributed)
nodes.rationale: Bundled minio and kafka are disabled in favour of the cluster's Rook RGW S3; priorityClassName feather-high is injected onto every chart Deployment/StatefulSet via post-render label-selector patches because the chart has no global field for it. HA-tracker/dedup was removed because metrics now arrive via clustered Alloy, which shards scrape targets instead of scraping everything twice, so there are no duplicate __replica__-tagged samples left to deduplicate.

nodes.label: Mimir tenant series and ingestion-rate limits
nodes.rationale: max_global_series_per_user 150k was exhausted (err-mimir-max-series-per-user silently rejected new series, blocking envoy metrics); 400k covers the in-memory head plus ~275k active series, temporarily raised to 600k on 2026-07-13 after an alloy-metrics clustering bug had both replicas scraping undeduplicated for ~2.5h. ingestion_rate raised from the 10000/s default to 30000 after new metrics sources (otis/vulpes-backend/reposilite OTel, envoy span-metrics, tempo local-blocks) triggered err-mimir-tenant-max-ingestion-rate, whose 429 backpressure cascaded into err-mimir-sample-timestamp-too-old and dropped unrelated pre-existing metrics.

nodes.label: eg Gateway in namespace envoy (https listener)
rook-ceph-rgw-feather-s3.rook-ceph-fr01.svc internal RGW S3 endpoint
nodes.rationale: Internal RGW service used path-style over plain http, deliberately decoupled from the external s3.onelitefeather.net ingress path.

nodes.label: alloy-receiver.grafana.svc OTLP gateway (:4317 grpc)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over pointing at tempo-gateway directly (as traces-only otis/vulpes-backend do) because this workload also needs metrics fanned out to Mimir, which only alloy-receiver's OTLP gateway does.

nodes.label: post-render kustomize injection of chart-unsupported pod fields
nodes.rationale: Charts that expose no field for priorityClassName (or whose podLabels leak into an immutable Deployment selector) are patched after rendering with a HelmRelease postRenderers kustomize JSON6902 patch, which touches only the pod template.

nodes.label: fr-rosenau region / fr01 zone node affinity convention

hyperedges.label: Public app exposure via Cloudflare Tunnel Ingress instead of chart ingress/HTTPRoute
Loki/Mimir object storage on the internal Rook RGW endpoint with SOPS-provided S3 credentials
Internal *.apps.onelite.feather routing of observability gateways through the eg Envoy Gateway https listener
